window.administratorHint: The Poros core runs with administrator rights: TUN and the kill switch with TUN turn on without asking for rights. The Poros window runs without them.

killSwitchHint.connected: Kill switch on connection: if the connection to the server drops, VPN traffic does not go directly until you press Stop. Click to open its setting.
killSwitchHint.always: Kill switch always: while Poros runs, VPN traffic goes only through the server and is closed without a connection. Click to open its setting.

killSwitchBlocking.held: The kill switch blocks VPN traffic now: the connection to the server dropped. Poros refuses in place of the server, and what the preset sends directly works. Stop opens all traffic without the VPN. Click to open the kill switch setting.
killSwitchBlocking.heldFull: The kill switch blocks the whole internet now: the Poros core restarted without rights, and TUN is down. Until it is back, Windows lets only Poros and the local network out. Connect again with rights or press Stop to open the internet without the VPN. Click to open the kill switch setting.
killSwitchBlocking.always: The kill switch blocks VPN traffic now: there is no connection, and in Always VPN traffic goes only through the server. Poros refuses in place of the server, and what the preset sends directly works. Connect so that the traffic goes through the server. Click to open the kill switch setting.
killSwitchBlocking.alwaysFull: The kill switch blocks the whole internet now: the Poros core restarted without rights, and TUN is down. Until it is back, Windows lets only Poros and the local network out. Connect again with rights. Click to open the kill switch setting.

tray.blockedAlways: VPN traffic closed until you connect

boot.notAnswering: The Poros core is not answering. If it stays so, Poros restarts it by itself.
boot.downHint: Connecting and the settings are unavailable until the core starts.
boot.damaged: The data file of Poros is damaged, as a sudden power cut may leave it. Poros can start with clean data: the subscriptions and settings will have to be added again, and the old file stays in the data folder.

logs.title: Log
logs.empty: The log is empty so far.

about.all: Everything goes through the server, the local network directly.
about.hardened: Like All traffic, plus TLS fragmentation. Helps when the connection keeps breaking.

wizard.tagline: Quick setup takes less than a minute.

subscription.title: Add a subscription
subscription.text: Paste the link from your provider, and Poros will load its servers. It usually comes in an email or from a bot after payment.
subscription.label: Subscription link

start.title: How to start Poros
start.autostartHint: Poros opens when you sign in.
start.autoConnectHint: Right after it starts, Poros connects to the server that worked last time.
start.urlSchemeHint: A link from a site or a messenger opens straight in Poros.
start.note: Windows keeps autostart and links outside the Poros folder. They can be turned off in the settings.

routing.title: Which traffic goes through the server
routing.note: The preset can be changed at any time on the main screen.

portal.lockTitle: Kill switch: VPN traffic goes only through the server

hint.both: TUN takes all of the computer's traffic through the server, and System also points programs at the proxy directly.
hint.tun: All of the computer's traffic goes through the server, games and programs included.
hint.system: Browsers and programs that use the system proxy go through the server.
hint.none: Without TUN and System only programs set to the proxy {address} go through the server.

portal.blockedAlways: VPN traffic closed until you connect
portal.heldTitle: The kill switch keeps VPN traffic from going out directly until the connection is back. What the preset sends directly still works. Stop lets all traffic out without the VPN.
portal.heldFullTitle: The Poros core restarted without rights, and TUN is not running: until it is back, Windows closes the whole internet except Poros and the local network. Connect again with rights, or press Stop to open the internet without the VPN.

list.emptyText: Paste a subscription link, and its servers will show up here.
list.removeText: “{name}” and its servers will be gone from Poros.
list.trafficLow: The subscription's traffic is running out: {left} of {total} left.
list.trafficOut: The subscription's traffic is used up. Providers usually turn the servers off until it is renewed.
list.endingSoon: The subscription ends {when}, on {date}. Renew it with the provider.
list.ended: The subscription ended on {date}. Providers usually turn the servers off until it is renewed.

add.title: Add a subscription
add.name: Name
add.note: The subscription shows up on the main screen as a group of its own.

modes.title: How traffic goes through the server
modes.tun: All of the computer's traffic, games and programs without proxy settings included. Needs administrator rights.
modes.system: Browsers and programs that use the Windows system proxy. No rights needed.
modes.note: Both can be on. The choice is remembered; the switches are on the main screen under Start.

admin.title: TUN needs administrator rights
admin.text: TUN creates a network adapter in Windows, which only an administrator may do. The Poros core restarts with rights and connects to the server right away.
admin.failed: TUN did not start without administrator rights.
admin.spoofFailed: TLS spoofing did not start without administrator rights, which its WinDivert driver needs.
admin.killSwitchTitle: The kill switch with TUN needs administrator rights
admin.killSwitchText: In the Always mode Poros keeps TUN up even without a connection, so that VPN traffic does not go around the server. TUN creates a network adapter in Windows, which only an administrator may do.
admin.killSwitchFailed: The kill switch did not turn on without administrator rights.

killSwitch.broken: The kill switch is not working, so VPN traffic can go out directly. The reason is in the log.

updates.killSwitch: The kill switch is off during the restart.
updates.reconnect: The connection comes back by itself.

failed.busy: The update to {version} did not install: a file is held by another program. Poros runs the previous version.
failed.damaged: The update to {version} did not install: the archive is damaged. Poros runs the previous version.
failed.failed: The update to {version} did not install. Poros runs the previous version; the reason is in the log.

proxy.title: Local proxy
proxy.lead: {address} is the proxy of Poros on this computer. A program set to it goes online by the rules of the preset: through the server or directly.
proxy.how: Set it in the program's settings, usually under Proxy or Network: type HTTP or SOCKS5, address {host}, port {port}. Or copy a ready link:
proxy.modes: TUN and System do this by themselves: TUN for every program, System for those that take the Windows proxy, such as browsers.
proxy.lan: Devices in your network can connect to port {port} too, at this computer's address in the local network.
proxy.lanOff: Only this computer can connect. For a phone or TV to go online through Poros, turn on “Let other devices connect” in Connection.

ip.title: IP and DNS
ip.connectFirst: Connect to see the exit address.
ip.unknown: The address could not be found.
ip.dns: DNS servers that see your queries
ip.noConnection: DNS leaks are checked through the connection. Press Start, and the check runs by itself.
ip.noLeakText: Only DNS servers on the VPN side see your queries.
ip.leakText: Some queries go past the server, and your provider sees which sites you open. Turn on TUN or a preset with DNS through the server.
ip.unknownLeak: A leak cannot be told: the provider without VPN is unknown.
ip.note: To check, Poros resolves a few random names and asks an outside service which DNS servers asked for them.
ip.off: The IP and DNS check is off in the settings.

restart.chipHint: The settings are saved but not applied to the connection. Click to restart it.
restart.title: Settings not applied
restart.text: The settings are saved, but the running connection still uses the old ones. To apply them, the connection has to restart: it drops for a couple of seconds.

presets.lead: A preset decides which traffic goes through the server and which goes directly. Built-in presets do not change: to add your own settings, make a copy or a new preset.
presets.none: No presets of your own yet.
presets.removeText: “{name}” will be gone. If it is chosen, Poros goes back to “{base}”.
presets.exportedLocal: The preset link is copied. Endpoints and the rules to them are profiles of this computer and stay out of the link.

conn.lead: How Poros connects and what it does when the connection breaks. TUN and System are on the main screen.

killSwitchHint.off: The internet is not blocked, even if the connection to the server breaks.
killSwitchHint.connected: If the connection to the server breaks, VPN traffic does not go out directly until you press Stop. The rest of the internet works.
killSwitchHint.always: While Poros runs, VPN traffic goes only through the server and is closed without a connection. The rest of the internet works. With TUN, needs administrator rights from the start.

conn.allowLanHint: A phone or TV on this network can go out through Poros. On the first connection Windows Firewall asks about PorosCore: allow it on private networks.
conn.checkIpHint: Before and after connecting, Poros asks an outside service for the IP and DNS servers. Click the IP for details and DNS leaks.
conn.ipv6Hint: Off, sites open over IPv4 only, and IPv6 connections do not go past the server.
conn.realityHint: VLESS servers with REALITY run on Xray. Off, they run on sing-box.
conn.killSwitchNote: How the kill switch works: VPN traffic is what the preset sends through the server. If the connection breaks, Poros keeps TUN and System on and refuses in place of the server: sites and programs the preset sends directly still work. With TUN, while the Poros core restarts, Windows closes the whole internet except Poros and the local network. Stop lifts the kill switch in the While connected mode, and so does choosing Off.

dns.lead: How Poros learns the addresses of sites and who sees these queries.
dns.serversHint: Presets with “Default” take them, the built-in ones too. A preset may choose its own.
dns.remoteHint: Queries go through the server; your provider does not see them.
dns.routingHint: Which way Poros learns the addresses of sites.
dns.routingNote: “As traffic”: a site’s name resolves the way its traffic goes, through the server for sites over VPN and directly for direct ones. “All through the server”: your provider sees no name, but direct sites may get CDN addresses far from you. “All direct”: faster, but your provider sees every name, those of sites over VPN too. While the kill switch holds back the server’s traffic, “All through the server” works as “As traffic”: otherwise direct sites would not open either.
dns.fakeIpHint: Works with TUN. Rules by site name match more precisely.
dns.fakeIpNote: Programs get an address of 198.18.0.0/15 at once instead of the real one, and Poros knows the site by it and routes it by the rules. Sites open a little faster. Some programs do not work with such addresses; then turn FakeIP off.
dns.hostsHint: Names of the Windows hosts file are answered as without Poros, with TUN too.
dns.answersHint: One per line: a name and one or more addresses separated by spaces. They answer before hosts and DNS servers.
dns.cacheHint: How many answers to keep and how long to wait for a server.
dns.objectHint: A whole sing-box dns object instead of the settings of this page.
dns.objectSet: An own DNS object is set: the settings of this page and the DNS of presets do not apply.
dns.objectSetSimple: An own DNS object is set in the advanced mode: the settings of this page and the DNS of presets do not apply.

subs.lead: How the server list is updated.
subs.viaProxyHint: Helps when the provider's site cannot be reached directly.
subs.showChangesHint: After an update by hand, show which servers came and went.
subs.deviceInfoHint: Needed by providers that limit the number of devices.
subs.deviceDataHint: Replace what Poros tells providers with “Send device data”. A group may have its own.

start.lead: The same as the Start step of quick setup.
start.startMinimizedHint: The window does not open, Poros stays in the tray.
start.closeToTray: Hide to the tray on close
start.closeToTrayHint: Off, the close button quits Poros.
start.urlSchemeOther: Another copy of Poros opens them now: {program}. Turn on to let this one open them.
start.autostartOnly: Works when Poros starts with Windows.
start.adminAutostartHint: At sign-in, TUN and the kill switch come on without asking for rights. Poros creates a Task Scheduler task for this, and Windows asks for permission once.
start.runAsAdminHint: Windows asks for permission at every start, and then TUN and the kill switch ask nothing. The Poros window runs without rights.
start.urlSchemeThis: poros:// links open in this copy of Poros.
start.urlSchemeOtherCopy: poros:// links open in another copy of Poros: {program}.
start.urlSchemeNone: poros:// links are not set up: from a browser they will not open in Poros.

look.lead: Language and size of the interface.

help.wizardHint: Go through the first-start steps again.
help.logsHint: What Poros did and what went wrong. The files are in the config\logs folder next to the program.
help.resetHint: Restarts the core if TUN stopped working.
help.ready: Version {version} is downloaded and ready to install.
help.checkFailed: The update check did not work. Current version: {version}.
help.local: A local build without a version does not update itself.
help.noUpdater: Current version: {version}. Without updater.exe next to it this build does not update itself.
help.autoCheckHint: At launch and every 4 hours. An update installs only when you press the button.
help.debugLogHint: Records every connection through Poros. Errors are always recorded. Takes effect with the next connection.
help.debugInfoHint: Versions of the cores, the system and the settings, without links and keys.
help.dataFolderHint: Poros keeps its data next to the program.
help.betaHint: Beta versions come out earlier and may work worse.

inbound.portHint: The port listens on 127.0.0.1, and on every address of the computer with “Allow other devices to connect” on the “Connection” page.
inbound.authHint: Ask programs that connect to the port for a name and password. The Windows system proxy passes no password, so Poros opens a port of its own for it, on this computer only.

tun.routingHint: Subnets the preset sends direct are excluded at the level of Windows routes and go around the TUN. Rules above them by program or port no longer apply to these subnets.
tun.bypassHint: They go around the TUN unless a rule sends them through the server. One per line; loopback and broadcast always go around.

protocols.fragmentHint: The ClientHello leaves in several TCP packets, and a blocker does not read the SNI. Not for REALITY and QUIC.
protocols.spoofHint: Needs administrator rights, the WinDivert driver. Only for servers with a name in the SNI.
protocols.quicHint: For Hysteria, Hysteria2, TUIC and MASQUE. Empty is the core’s own.

net.ignoreTlsHint: In the requests of Poros itself: subscriptions, the IP check. Updates are always checked: what they download runs.
net.ntpHint: A clock of the core’s own, for when the system time is wrong.

security.systemCerts: Trust the system certificates in Xray
security.systemCertsHint: Xray takes the certificates of Windows, such as corporate ones, instead of its own list.
security.insecure: Skip the TLS check by default (allowInsecure)
security.insecureHint: For profiles without a check of their own; pinned certificates of a profile are still checked. Xray always checks.

logging.linesHint: From 100 to 20,000. How much the log records, “Detailed log” in “Help” says.
logging.statsHint: Traffic counters for “Connections”, “Statistics” and the speed. Turned off, there are none. Takes effect with the next connection.
logging.historyHint: By profile and application, 90 days, in a database of its own, for “Statistics → Traffic”.
logging.historyNeedsStats: Works with the statistics of connections.

linkPreset.title: Add the preset from the link?
linkPreset.text: The preset “{name}” goes to “My presets”. The preset in use does not change.

presetEdit.name: Name
presetEdit.defaultHint: Where everything goes that no rule below takes.
presetEdit.defaultBlocked: Only the sites and programs of the rules will work. Poros blocks the rest.
presetEdit.dnsRemoteHint: Queries go through the server. “Default” is as in “Settings → DNS”.
presetEdit.dnsDirectHint: Queries go past the server. “Default” is as in “Settings → DNS”.
presetEdit.dnsCustomHint: https://, tls:// or an IP address
presetEdit.builtinNote: A built-in preset does not change. To add rules of your own, make a copy.
presetEdit.dnsObject: An own DNS object is set: the DNS of presets does not apply.
presetEdit.warpOff: WARP is off, so “Through WARP” goes through the server for now. It turns on in “Routing → WARP”.
presetEdit.warpOffSimple: WARP is off, so “Through WARP” goes through the server for now. It turns on in “Routing → WARP” of the advanced mode.

presetLists.title: Lists of “{name}”
presetLists.hint: Every line starts with a prefix: suffix: is a site with its subdomains, ip: an IP or a subnet, processName: a program, processPath: the path to a program. Lines starting with # are not read.
presetLists.locked: Locked rules, rules of several conditions and rules to endpoints stay out of here. New lines go to the end of the list.
presetLists.invalid: {n} line not recognized: {lines}. Fix or remove it. | {n} lines not recognized: {lines}. Fix or remove them.
presetLists.duplicate: Already on other tabs: {lines}. Keep each line on one tab only.
presetLists.hintAdvanced: Every line starts with a prefix: suffix: is a site with its subdomains, ip: an IP or a subnet, processName: a program, processPath: the path to a program; an advanced preset adds domain: for an exact domain, keyword:, regex:, processPathRegex:, port:, protocol:, network:, ipVersion:, sourceIP:. Lines starting with # are not read.
presetLists.advancedOnly: this kind belongs to an advanced preset

rules.title: Rules
rules.hint: Checked from the top; the first that matches decides. A narrower rule rises over a wider one of the same kind by itself: ads.example.com over example.com.

invalid.ip: neither an address nor a subnet
invalid.processPath: not a path to a program
invalid.port: neither a port nor a range
invalid.sourceIP: neither an address nor a subnet

problem.advanced: Only an advanced preset has this.

dialog.title: Rule
dialog.name: Name
dialog.conditionsHint: The rule matches when all its conditions do; a condition matches by any of its values, one per line.
dialog.invertHint: The rule takes everything its conditions do not match.

endpoints.hint: OpenVPN and OpenConnect profiles connect alongside the server while this preset runs. The networks they announce go through them, by the locked rule “Endpoint networks”; rules send them other traffic. If an endpoint does not connect, Start fails and says why.
endpoints.noProfiles: There are no OpenVPN or OpenConnect profiles
endpoints.goneHint: It is no longer there: remove the endpoint, or Start fails.
endpoints.removeText: {n} rules to “{name}” will send their traffic through the server. | {n} rule to “{name}” will send its traffic through the server. | {n} rules to “{name}” will send their traffic through the server.

dnsCache.title: Cache and timeouts
dnsCache.cacheHint: A repeated query of the same name does not go to the DNS server.
dnsCache.ignoreTtlHint: An answer stays in the cache until newer ones push it out.
dnsCache.optimisticHint: An outdated answer is given at once, and a fresh one is asked for in the background.
dnsCache.optimisticOff: Not together with “Ignore the lifetime of answers”: answers do not get outdated then.
dnsCache.timeoutHint: How many seconds to wait for a DNS server to answer.
dnsCache.subnetHint: Optional. Tells DNS servers where a query comes from, so that CDNs give near addresses.
dnsCache.wrongSize: The cache size is a whole number from 1 to 1048576.
dnsCache.wrongTimeout: The timeout is a whole number of seconds from 1 to 60.

dnsObject.title: Own DNS object
dnsObject.hint: The whole dns object of a sing-box config. While it is set, the settings of the DNS page and the DNS of presets do not apply. Servers with "detour": "proxy" go through the VPN. The addresses of servers resolve with the dns-direct server, or with the system DNS without one.
dnsObject.label: DNS object

newPreset.title: New preset
newPreset.name: New preset
newPreset.simpleText: Sites, IPs and programs: through the server, directly or blocked. Enough for almost everyone.
newPreset.advancedText: Adds rules of several conditions, ports and protocols, WARP, OpenVPN and OpenConnect endpoints and a direct DNS of your own.
newPreset.note: A simple preset can become advanced later, but not back.

toAdvanced.title: Make the preset advanced?
toAdvanced.text: The preset “{name}” gets all the settings of an advanced one: rules of several conditions, ports and protocols, WARP, endpoints and a direct DNS. Its rules stay as they are.
toAdvanced.warn: The preset cannot become simple again.

common.title: General
common.addressFirst: Which address of a site to take first
common.addressFirstHint: If a site has both. With IPv6 off on the “Connection” page, IPv4 only.
common.presetHint: The same choice as in the connection bar.

warp.title: WARP
warp.useHint: Traffic with the “Through WARP” action goes out to the internet through Cloudflare WARP after the server: the site sees an address of Cloudflare. Helps with services that do not accept VPN addresses. Turned off, this traffic goes through the server.
warp.none: No configuration: get one from Cloudflare or enter your own.
warp.modeHint: MASQUE goes over HTTP/3 or HTTP/2 and helps when UDP does not pass through the server.
warp.termsText: Poros will register a new WARP device with Cloudflare and write its keys to this page. While Poros is connected, the request goes through the server.
warp.termsTextReplace: Poros will register a new WARP device with Cloudflare and write its keys to this page instead of the current ones. While Poros is connected, the request goes through the server.
warp.terms: This requires accepting the Cloudflare WARP terms of use:
warp.hostsHint: One per line. Poros tries them in order if the first is unreachable. Empty means api.cloudflareclient.com.

reason.port_busy: port 2090 is taken by another program
reason.port_poros: port 2090 is taken by another Poros on this computer, such as one of another Windows user
reason.tun_taken: another Poros on this computer, such as one of another Windows user, has its TUN on. Windows has one set of routes for everyone, so only one can have a TUN: connect through System
reason.kill_switch_taken: another Poros on this computer, such as one of another Windows user, holds a kill switch with TUN. Two blocks of Windows would shut out each other's connection, so this one did not turn on
reason.tun_busy: Windows still holds the TUN adapter of an earlier start. Try again; if that does not help, restart Windows
reason.system_proxy_failed: the system proxy could not be set
reason.server_unsupported: Poros cannot connect to this server
reason.kill_switch_needs_elevation: the kill switch needs administrator rights
reason.logon_task_needs_elevation: rights at autostart need administrator rights
reason.logon_task_failed: Windows did not create the Task Scheduler task
reason.kill_switch_failed: the kill switch did not turn on
reason.stop_timeout: the connection did not close in time; reset it in Help
reason.invalid_subscription: this does not look like a subscription
reason.no_servers: the subscription has no servers Poros can connect to
reason.invalid_url: a subscription link starts with http:// or https://
reason.single_server: This is a link to one server, not a subscription. Poros adds subscriptions only for now.
reason.subscription_url: this is a subscription link: add it as a subscription
reason.not_manual: servers go only to a group of your own, not to a subscription
reason.check_failed: a part of the check failed
reason.invalid_entry: the value does not fit its kind
reason.invalid_link: this is no Poros preset link
reason.update_failed: the update check did not work
reason.update_unavailable: this build does not update itself
reason.update_not_ready: no update is downloaded, or it changed after the download
reason.core_timeout: the Poros core did not answer in time
reason.core_start_failed: the Poros core did not start
reason.preset_name_taken: a preset of this name exists already
reason.check_off: the IP and DNS check is off in the settings
reason.advanced_only: only an advanced preset has this
reason.endpoint_failed: an endpoint of the preset did not connect

links.unknown: Poros does not know this link: {link}

mode.simpleHint: Simple mode: the main settings for every day. Click to move to the advanced mode.
mode.advancedHint: Advanced mode: every setting and feature of Poros. Click to move to the simple mode.
mode.toAdvancedText: The advanced mode opens every setting and feature of Poros: your own groups and profiles, the profile editor, routing rules, connections, statistics and tools.
mode.toSimpleText: The simple mode keeps the main things: servers, presets and the basic settings. Everything set up in the advanced mode stays and keeps working.
mode.note: The connection keeps running. You can come back the same way, with the mode chip in the title bar or from the menu.

adv.soon: This section is still being built and comes in one of the next builds.

logs.badRegex: The regular expression has a mistake: all lines are shown.

connections.filter: Filter by process, address or outbound
connections.idle: Not connected. Connections show up after Start.
connections.untracked: The statistics of connections are off: without them Poros neither counts the traffic of connections nor knows their programs.
connections.closeProcess: Close the connections of the process

traffic.off: The traffic history is off: new traffic does not come here.

profiles.newSubscriptionText: A subscription comes from a provider by a link and updates itself.
profiles.newGroupText: A group of your own holds profiles added by hand.
profiles.noGroups: No subscriptions and no groups of your own yet.
profiles.manualText: Your own group, profiles added by hand
profiles.enterLinkPlaceholder: Links one per line, a subscription in base64, Clash, sing-box or Xray JSON, a .ovpn or WireGuard file
profiles.testLatencyGroup: Test the delay of the group
profiles.testSpeedGroup: Measure the speed of the group
profiles.testIpGroup: Find the exit IP of the group
profiles.resolveGroup: Resolve the domains of the group
profiles.cleaned: No profiles removed | {n} profile removed | {n} profiles removed
profiles.name: Name

security.weak: Weak protection: an old cipher or TLS that checks no certificate.
security.none: No encryption: the traffic to the server can be seen on its way.

profiles.moveTitle: Move {n} profiles | Move the profile | Move {n} profiles
profiles.moveText: Profiles of your own group move to the other one; profiles of a subscription are copied, as its update would bring them back.
profiles.removeTitle: Remove {n} profiles? | Remove the profile? | Remove {n} profiles?
profiles.removeTextSubscription: The profiles leave the subscription until its next update.
profiles.copiedLinks: No links copied | {n} link copied | {n} links copied
profiles.copiedConfigs: No configs copied | The config is copied | {n} configs copied
profiles.resolved: No domains found | The domain of {n} profile is now its address | The domains of {n} profiles are now their addresses
profiles.addedSkipped: Added: {added}. Not added: {skipped}, which cannot run or are broken.
profiles.linkTitle: Add the server from the link?
profiles.linkText: The link from a browser or a messenger leads to one server.

groupEditor.title: Group
groupEditor.name: Name
groupEditor.proxiesHint: The front proxy is a server Poros reaches the servers of the group through; the landing proxy one the traffic leaves by after them.
groupEditor.copyLinks: Copy the links of the profiles
groupEditor.addressHint: A host or IP for every server of the group, such as an IP of a CDN. The server name stays in SNI.
groupEditor.keepWorkingHint: Profiles whose test worked stay, even when the subscription no longer has them.
groupEditor.byTest: By the results of the URL test.

profileEditor.title: Profile
profileEditor.problem: The core will not start the profile: {problem}
profileEditor.jsonNoType: A profile is a JSON object with a type field
profileEditor.jsonHint: The profile as Poros stores it. The core checks it as you type; errors show under the tabs.

tls.certificatePin: SHA-256 of the certificate in base64, split by commas
tls.publicKeyPin: SHA-256 of the server key in base64, split by commas
tls.spoofSni: Empty takes the one of “Protocols and bypass”
tls.disableSni: TLS spoofing does not work without the SNI.

transport.headers: One header a line: Name: value

ssh.hostKey: Split by commas; empty accepts any key

openvpn.fingerprint: SHA-256 of the server certificate, split by commas

chain.servers: The first server is dialled directly, each next one through the one before

custom.json: One sing-box outbound or endpoint with its own type, server and server_port
